objective: Implement a case-level detector evaluation, select settings using only the exploration split, and explain the limits of the resulting synthetic counts and rates.
question: Implement classify(signals, settings) and evaluate(cases, settings) in evaluation/policy.mjs. Count distant range denials inside any open-left, closed-right tick window, predict without reading labels, and compute one confusion-matrix vote per case. Record your settings before the evaluation run, preserve your first predictions and assistance in response.md, and explain the legal honest/automation twin and undefined rates. Compare exploration windows 8 and 20 at threshold 3 and minimum distance 500 before committing settings. Append repairs without replacing earlier answers.
constraints: The only submitted executable file is evaluation/policy.mjs. Keep it independent of files, clocks, network APIs and reference code.

Inputs are validated. A signal is {tick,reason,distanceSquared}; signals have nonnegative integer ticks in nondecreasing order, reason range or cooldown, and nonnegative finite squared distances. Equal-tick observations may occur. Do not mutate inputs.
Settings are {threshold,windowTicks,minDistanceMm}; threshold and windowTicks are positive integers and minDistanceMm is finite and nonnegative.
An observation is eligible only when reason equals range and distanceSquared is strictly greater than minDistanceMm squared. Cooldown and near-boundary denials do not count.

classify returns a Boolean. Flag if any interval (latest-windowTicks, latest] contains at least threshold eligible observations. The exact left edge is excluded. A later quiet period does not erase an earlier qualifying interval.

Each case is {id,label,signals}, with a unique id and Boolean synthetic label. evaluate returns exactly {decisions,metrics}; decisions preserves input order as {id,flagged}. Labels are used only after predictions for scoring, never as classification features.

Metrics are {total,tp,fp,tn,fn,precision,recall,falsePositiveRate}. Count every case once, including a case with many observations. precision=tp/(tp+fp), recall=tp/(tp+fn), falsePositiveRate=fp/(fp+tn). A zero denominator produces null, never zero or NaN.

Use only the stable exploration IDs to choose settings. Record settings and policy source identity before running the separate evaluation IDs. Keep the corpus and source hashes with the report; do not tune on the evaluation results and report them as a fresh evaluation.

The corpus is fourteen scripted controls from the owned local game. Its author-assigned violation label is true only for repeated-distant-invalid behavior; declaredAutomation is separate metadata never supplied as a policy feature. It contains no human participants. Its counts and rates do not estimate real-human behavior, production prevalence or operational false-positive rates. A flag is advisory, never an automatic ban.
assessment: Owner-side fixtures check window boundaries, eligible observations, one-case-one-vote metrics, decision order, label independence and undefined rates. Two independently structured correct policies pass; at least six plausible wrong policies fail with expected/actual feedback and a teaching source. The separate real-engine corpus demonstrates window tradeoffs and an indistinguishable legal honest/valid-automation pair without treating automation as a rule violation; it is not held-out human learning evidence.
